One foot turns out more than the other and nobody ever checks which way your pelvis is facing If one of your feet turns out more than the other, you’ve probably tried pointing it straight or doing calf stretches. But that foot isn’t turned out because of the foot. It’s turned out because of where your pelvis is sitting. When your pelvis rotates toward one side, the leg on that side externally rotates with it. The foot turns out and loses the ability to pronate, the natural inward roll it needs every time you take a step. A 2007 study in Gait and Posture tested 35 healthy subjects and found that forces at the foot significantly altered alignment all the way up through the hip and pelvis. The chain works both directions. If the pelvis is turned, the foot follows. Forcing that foot straight doesn’t undo the rotation. It just jams the ankle and knee into a position they can’t sustain. The fix has three parts. First, teach that foot to pronate again by reaching your knee and arm forward in a lunge position. Slow, about 15 reps. Second, open up the opposite side of the pelvis with a stretch and long breathing. Third, teach the hip on the turned-out side to actually rotate the other direction with a glute engagement hold, about 15 breaths. If that turned-out foot has been there for years and nobody has connected it to your pelvis, comment RELIEF below and I’ll get you pointed in the right direction. Especially if it’s been messing with your running, your hiking, or any activity where one side always feels off. #footpronation #pelvis #hippain
